subject: Dedicated capacity recap & next steps (Acme Health)
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
To: James Li <james.li@acmehealth.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwoodinference.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Thu, 1 Apr 2027 15:05:00 -0700
Subject: Dedicated capacity recap & next steps (Acme Health)

Hi James —

Thanks again for the time today. Quick recap from our discovery so we’re all aligned and have clear next steps. Please reply if I missed anything.

Summary of pain points
- Production latency spikes on peak-hour inference for clinical triage (95th percentile currently ~750ms, target <200ms)
- Concerns about data isolation and PHI handling for test/prod separation
- Need predictable unit economics for budgeting (avoid token cost variability)

Goals you shared
- Dedicated GPU capacity with isolation (VPC + tenant isolation)
- Support for a mixed workload: real-time inference (low latency) + batch reranking overnight
- SLA needs: uptime + latency targets for internal SLAs, willingness to commit to a minimum capacity for better pricing

Redwood dedicated recommendation (high level)
- Reserved footprint: 8x H100-class GPUs (can size to A100 alternative if preferred) for primary capacity; autoscale policy to allow up to +50% burst on shared pools for short periods
- Isolation: Customer VPC + dedicated tenant plane, KV/prefix caching scoped per environment; optional on-prem connector for sensitive workloads
- Network/residency: deploy in us-west-2 with private peering (we can scope for multi-region DR if needed)
- SLA targets: 99.95% uptime and 95th percentile <250ms for provisioned capacity (we’ll surface exact SLOs in SOW)

Attachments: redwood_dedicated_proposal_acme_20270401.pdf (proposal + ballpark pricing)

Next steps
1) I’ll share a capacity worksheet and preliminary SOW for your review (attached).
2) Rishi/Neha to run a short technical deep-dive next week to validate sizing and network requirements — propose Tue 2027-04-05 10:00am PT.
3) If the sizing looks good, we’ll produce a formal SOW and contract with a target turnaround of 7–10 business days.

Action items for Acme
- Confirm that 8x H100 is in the right sizing ballpark or provide peak qps/seq len metrics so we can refine
- Share any security questionnaire or SOC2 artifacts you need early in the process

Thanks — looking forward to moving this forward.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Enterprise Sales | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com | +1 (415) 555-0192

Date: Fri, 2 Apr 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity recap & next steps (Acme Health)

Thanks Marissa — helpful recap. A few clarifications from our side: 

- Data residency and PHI isolation are hard requirements for prod workloads. We need assurances around tenant isolation + KMS integration.
- SLA: we’re targeting 99.95% uptime and a 95th latency of <200ms for user-facing triage. If those are achievable with committed capacity, we can move fast.
- Cost: can you give a ballpark monthly cost for the 8x H100 reserved footprint (include support/SLA premium)? We need a budget number for procurement.

Also, Tue 4/5 10am PT works for a tech deep-dive; I’ll loop in our infra lead (infra@acmehealth.com) with network/firewall questions.

Thanks,
James
Head of Platform Engineering | Acme Health
james.li@acmehealth.com

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
To: James Li <james.li@acmehealth.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwoodinference.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Fri, 2 Apr 2027 11:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity recap & next steps (Acme Health)

James — appreciate the clarity. Quick responses inline and a few concrete items attached.

- PHI + isolation: we support customer-managed KMS and provide a dedicated tenant plane + VPC peering for Dedicated customers. We will include SOC2 artifacts and our security integration checklist in the tech packet.
- SLA: we can commit to 99.95% uptime for reserved Dedicated capacity on a 12‑month reserved contract (SLA terms to be included in SOW). For latency, we will guarantee 95th <250ms on provisioned capacity; to meet <200ms at 95th we recommend the reserved + optimized kernel/quantization profile and a canary test to validate at your payload distribution. We’ll include a canary rollout plan in the SOW.
- Ballpark cost (monthly): $88,000/month for 8x H100 reserved capacity + enterprise support and SLA premium. This is a starting estimate — final pricing depends on contract length and any additional DR/multi-region needs.

Attachments: acme_capacity_worksheet.xlsx, prelim_sow_acme_20270402.docx

Proposed next steps
- Tech deep-dive Tue 2027-04-05 10:00am PT (I’ll send calendar invite after you confirm).
- Rishi/Neha to prepare a short canary plan and cost breakdown; Neha will lead the security artifact bundle.
- If Acme signs the SOW, we can target a staged rollout: 2-week onboarding + 2-week canary + full cutover within 6 weeks from signature (dependent on integrations).

If that looks good I’ll update the proposal with the SLA language and schedule the kickoff.

Best,
Marissa

- Rishi: can you prepare a canary rollout plan (2-week canary, metrics to monitor: 95th latency, p99, error rate, token cost delta) and a sizing verification checklist. Also include recommended autoscale thresholds for burst behavior.
- Neha: please compile SOC2 artifacts we can share and prepare KMS integration steps + network checklist for VPC peering.
- I’ll update the SOW to include 99.95% uptime and the provisional latency guidance; include the pricing line $88,000/mo as ballpark pending final sizing.

Attach the two docs I just sent to Acme to the calendar invite and include the HubSpot deal link (https://app.hubspot.com/deals/1234567/RDW-2319). We’ll aim to have the package ready before the call so procurement can move quickly.

Marissa
